headline: Growing far faster than the Big 4 by leading on digital platforms, fast application processing, and putting best rates forward upfront rather than requiring back-and-forth negotiation
reasoning: Clunes observes that Macquarie Bank is outperforming the major banks in mortgage market share by offering a superior digital broker platform, a fast application process, and transparent upfront pricing. Unlike other banks where brokers must negotiate rates back and forth, Macquarie offers its best rate immediately, making it easy for brokers to recommend. This approach is well-suited to the current environment where borrowers are actively refinancing, and the bank has found a strong niche in residential mortgages.
quote: Macquarie is very good at customer service, their digital platforms fantastic for brokers as well. It's a very fast application process, so they've analysed the market and they've found where they fit exceptionally well with residential mortgages and they have looked for every little bit of optimization they can find in that process. So when a borrower goes to Macquarie, as long as the parameters fit that particular borrower's circumstances, the moving is exceptionally easy and people are getting very good deals. There's not bartering like there is with some of the other banks where we have to go back and forth in terms of interest rates. Macquarie put their best rate forward upfront, which makes it very easy for us as brokers to recommend them as a product to borrowers.
episode_title: Mortgage competition heats up as lending falls

headline: Investors pivoting from heavily geared residential property toward higher-yielding commercial property and SMSF structures as rate pressures mount and distressed stock hits the market
reasoning: Clunes notes a notable shift in borrower behaviour away from negatively geared residential property toward commercial property and commercial property within self-managed superannuation funds. Rising mortgage costs for those who bought at low interest rates are pushing properties onto the market, and he sees opportunity for well-positioned buyers in the current downturn. Investors are now prioritising higher-yield assets over capital-growth plays that require significant leverage.
quote: In terms of movements in the property market, we're seeing a lot of borrowers move towards commercial property as well as commercial property within a self managed Superfund seems to be quite common. We're seeing borrowers who bought maybe when interest rates were very low, their mortgages have gone up significantly as well, which are putting pressures on their budget. So there's a lot of property that's starting to hit the market. And with the recent downturn, if you're in a position to do so, there's some very good buyers out there.
episode_title: Mortgage competition heats up as lending falls

headline: Auction clearance rates are likely to be the first indicator of a lending cycle floor, with larger lenders already beginning to loosen policies and push for new business
reasoning: Clunes argues the current downturn is not purely sentiment-driven but reflects a structural credit crunch stemming from the negative gearing changes. He expects the lending cycle to trough first when auction clearance rates begin rising. He also observes that in recent weeks some larger lenders have started to open their credit policies and actively seek new business, which should gradually allow more credit to flow into the market.
quote: I think it's going to appear first in the auction clearance rates. We may see those start to rise. It's, I don't think it's purely consumer sentiment driven this downturn. There's definitely a credit crunch like I mentioned with that reduction of negative gearing. But what we're seeing in the last couple of weeks especially is lenders and some of the bigger lenders as well opening their policies and starting to push a bit harder for some of that new business and that's going to start allowing more credit to flow.
episode_title: Mortgage competition heats up as lending falls

headline: Negative gearing reduction creating a credit crunch for residential property investors, cutting borrowing capacity 15–30% and driving a 65% year-on-year rise in non-bank lending
reasoning: Clunes identifies the reduction in negative gearing as a structural driver of the lending slowdown on the investor side, with borrowing capacity falling 15–30% for affected borrowers. This has caused a credit crunch particularly for those seeking one to three investment properties, many of whom can no longer clear serviceability hurdles. However, non-bank lenders with more open serviceability policies have stepped in, with non-bank lending up 65% year-on-year as major banks' volumes decline.
quote: Definitely on the investor side. So we're seeing a credit crunch in that investor market, primarily residential. And it's a little bit of something that people might not see because the change with the reduction of negative gearing, it reduces people's borrowing capacity by anywhere from 15 to 30%. So what it's created is a credit crunch with those particular borrowers that were looking to buy one investment property, maybe a second or third. They can no longer afford to do so. And that's only going to show up in mortgage volumes dropping as these borrowers can no longer clear the serviceability hurdles. It has been picked up, however. So the non bank lending year on year is up 65%.
episode_title: Mortgage competition heats up as lending falls

headline: 16% drop in mortgage enquiries and origination is creating significant borrower bargaining power to reprice existing loans or switch lenders
reasoning: Nicholas Clunes notes a 16% drop in mortgage enquiries and origination across the board, which has led to reduced lending volumes at major banks. This has created an environment where existing borrowers can renegotiate rates with their current lender or engage brokers to switch. He also notes approximately 1,800 borrowers (roughly $1 billion in mortgages) switch lenders every day, reflecting heightened borrower activity in search of better deals as household budgets tighten.
quote: So right now there's a big drive, especially with mortgage enquiries and origination down across the boards. There's been a 16% drop recently. There's a lot of ability to reprice. There's a lot of ability to speak with your existing lender. Existing lenders, especially some of the bigger banks, have seen their lending values decrease quite rapidly over the last couple of months with the credit crunch. So a lot of borrowers have the opportunity now to not only try and reprice their existing mortgages competitions a little bit higher, but also to speak to new lenders and to engage brokers to see if there's an opportunity to move their loan.
episode_title: Mortgage competition heats up as lending falls
